_note: The LED lesson of the learning journey (TRD addendum sections 4, 5 and 6.1). It fixes the reference circuit of Arduino Foundations level 2 with a version number. Change the version when the circuit, the code or the map changes. baseline.levels: the levels of content/boards/arduino-foundations.json that make the reference board. The reference code is the solution of the level 2 code step in content/sketches/arduino-foundations.json. map: one item for each terminal and each connection; the id is the stable id. The explain text tells the holes of the reference build. changes: the changes that the simulator shows correctly (supported: true, a challenge can use them), and two that it cannot show (supported: false, with the reason). ops changes the reference; model is what the simulator then shows. tests/observe.test.ts runs each change. schematic: the id of the element in components/journey/schematic-af-led.tsx that shows the terminal or the connection (Compare views, issue #202). The lesson has no media and no questions until the photos and the clip of the real circuit exist; lib/journey/questions.ts gives the shape of a question. The challenges come in work package 6. Write the text in ASD-STE100.

inventory.name: Wire from GND to the − line
Wire from pin 13 to the resistor
Wire from the LED to the − line

terminals.label: + line on the left of breadboard A
− line on the left of breadboard A

connections.explain: A wire takes 5 V from the Uno to the + line on the left of breadboard A. The 25 holes of this line connect inside the breadboard.
A wire connects GND of the Uno to the − line on the left of breadboard A. The 25 holes of this line connect inside the breadboard, so a part that touches the line touches ground.
A wire takes pin 13 to hole a22 of breadboard A. Holes a to e of column 22 connect inside the breadboard. The first leg of the resistor is in hole c22, so pin 13 touches the resistor.
The second leg of the resistor is in hole c26, and the long leg (+) of the LED is in hole e26. Holes a to e of column 26 connect inside the breadboard, so this connection needs no wire.
The short leg (−) of the LED is in hole e27. A wire goes from hole a27 to the − line, and the − line goes to GND. This closes the loop from pin 13 back to the Uno.

changes.text: Move the end of the pin 13 wire to pin 12.
Remove the wire from the LED to the − line.
Move the end of the LED wire from the − line to the + line.
Move the short leg (−) of the LED to the + line.
Put the resistor on the other side of the LED: pin 13 to the LED, then the resistor, then the − line.
Change each delay(500) in the sketch to delay(100).
Remove the resistor, and join its two holes with a wire.
changes.reason: The simulator shows the LED blink, but a real LED gets too much current and can burn. The simulator does not calculate current.

changes.text: A wire is loose in its hole.
changes.reason: In the simulator, a wire is in its hole or it is not. A real loose wire makes the LED flicker or stay off. Use the fault clip for this change.
